answer: Randomness-Gated Admission Windows. Each agent joins only through a slot opened by a public verifiable random function beacon; the rare slot is unguessable until revealed, so an attacker cannot precompute where to mass-register identities. Every attempt must pay a full admission fee, and each rejected or duplicate claim forfeits it to a shared oasis fund. Mass identity creation thus costs linear fees with no guaranteed success, while honest agents wait out a haven of scarce slots. A raven watcher audits slot reuse and slashes repeat claimants.
